theme: Monday: Tesla Robotaxi goes live in San Antonio, bitcoin slips under Strategy's cost as it buys 1,037 more BTC, Starship Flight 15 aims for a double catch Nov 13, Starlink prices rise, RKLB and ASTS report tonight with CoreWeave tomorrow, Anthropic's IPO roadshow starts, Taiwan's chip stocks surge, and October CPI is due Tuesday.

items.title: Where Tesla Robotaxi runs, metro by metro
items.picked: Tesla's Robotaxi went live in San Antonio at 5 a.m. local time today with a roughly 275-square-mile zone, its biggest yet, and Austin's area was expanded overnight, per Tesla's @robotaxi account and a story trending on X. This tab was updated this morning to include the launch.
items.matters: The number of metros where Tesla runs without anyone behind the wheel is the clearest scorecard for the robotaxi story behind much of Tesla's valuation. The table separates real unsupervised service from permits and plans.
items.know: The tab lists 11 metros: Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, Miami, Orlando and Tampa as ramping unsupervised, San Antonio as live since Nov 9 2026 with safety-monitor status unconfirmed by Tesla, the SF Bay Area with safety drivers only, and Las Vegas and Phoenix still in preparation. Fort Worth went unsupervised on Nov 2 2026. The image is rendered from the live sheet because the Nov 2 Drive export predates the Fort Worth and San Antonio rows.

items.title: Texas robotaxi registrations: Tesla vs Waymo
items.picked: Alongside today's San Antonio launch, a story trending on X says Texas DMV records now show 1,282 Tesla robotaxis vs 1,285 for Waymo, almost level. San Antonio is Tesla's eighth Robotaxi city.
items.matters: Texas is the one state where a public registry lets you count robotaxi fleets head to head. It shows whether Tesla's ramp is catching the market leader.
items.know: The tab's latest count, Oct 31 2026, has Tesla at 1,204 registered vehicles (631 Model Y and 573 Cybercabs) vs 1,259 for Waymo, 344 for Avride and 63 for Zoox. These are registered vehicles, not cars carrying riders, and today's reported 1,282 vs 1,285 isn't in the tab yet. The image's title still reads Tesla 1,080 vs Waymo 1,207 (Oct 28) from an earlier build.

items.title: Tesla Cybercabs on the Texas robotaxi registry
items.picked: Cybercabs are now running from 5 a.m. as Tesla stretched Robotaxi hours to 21 a day in Austin, Dallas and Tampa this weekend, and Musk is winding down Cybertruck production in mid-2027 to build more Cybercabs, per stories trending on X.
items.matters: Cybercab is the purpose-built robotaxi Tesla's network is supposed to scale on. Registrations are the most direct public count of how fast they're reaching the road.
items.know: Texas Cybercab registrations rose from 45 on Aug 31 to 573 on Oct 31 2026, the tab's latest check, including 544 on Oct 27. That's more than 12 times as many in two months. The data stops Oct 31, and the image's title still says 45 to 319, from an earlier build.

items.title: Bitcoin's price vs what ETFs, companies and Strategy paid
items.picked: Bitcoin traded around $73,700 to $74,800 this morning, below Strategy's $75,451 average cost, and a story trending on X says the company's paper gain has flipped to a loss. Strategy also disclosed this morning that it bought 1,037 more BTC.
items.matters: When bitcoin trades under the average price that big holders paid, their paper profits are gone. That level is now being watched as a test for ETF holders and treasury companies.
items.know: On Oct 14 2026, the tab's latest snapshot with bitcoin at $81,562, the average cost was $76,645 for US spot ETFs, $78,881 for all public companies, $80,382 for treasury companies, $75,444 for Strategy and $81,126 for BlackRock's IBIT. At today's prices all of those groups would be under water on average. The snapshot is almost four weeks old.

items.title: Strategy: bitcoin held vs its average purchase cost
items.picked: Strategy said this morning it bought 1,037 BTC for about $77 million, taking it to 850,364 BTC, with bitcoin now below its average cost, per a story trending on X. Saylor teased the buy on Sunday with his 'connecting the dots' chart.
items.matters: Strategy is the largest corporate holder, and its average cost is the line the market watches for stress at the company. This chart shows how close the price has come to that line.
items.know: On the tab's latest weekly point, Oct 30 2026, bitcoin was at $77,191 against Strategy's average cost of $75,446, with 848.5 thousand BTC held. The price last spent a long stretch below the cost line from late May to mid-August 2026, falling as low as $59,996 (Jun 26). The weekly data stops Oct 30, so this week's dip and today's purchase aren't in it.

items.title: Strategy's weekly bitcoin buys and sales
items.picked: Today's 1,037 BTC purchase is Strategy's latest weekly buy, funded partly by stock sales, per a story trending on X. It comes with the price under the company's cost basis.
items.matters: The size of each weekly buy shows how much new money Strategy can raise. The chart also shows the summer weeks when it sold bitcoin instead.
items.know: The ledger's latest entry is Oct 26 2026: 811 BTC at $80,846 average, taking holdings to 849,327 BTC. Strategy sold 6,948 BTC across five entries from Jun 1 to Aug 10 2026, then resumed buying on Aug 31 with 4,603 BTC. Since then buys have been small, from 250 to 1,665 BTC a week; today's 1,037 BTC isn't in the ledger yet.

items.title: Starship's 14 flight tests
items.picked: SpaceX is targeting Starship Flight 15 as early as Nov 13 from Starbase, aiming to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the ship at the tower, per stories trending on X. It would be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket.
items.matters: Full reuse of both stages is what would make Starship cheap enough to launch Starlink V3 and SpaceX's space data center plans at scale. This record shows how far the program has come and where it still fails.
items.know: Of 14 flights, 9 reached their planned trajectory and the booster was caught three times (Flights 5, 7 and 8). The last three Block 3 boosters didn't get caught: Flights 12 and 13 failed in the Gulf and Flight 14 did a controlled splashdown. Flight 14 on Sep 28 2026 was the first to reach orbit, carrying 26 Starlink V3. The ship has never been caught. The tab was built Oct 9 2026.

items.title: Starlink capacity added per launch: Falcon 9 vs Starship
items.picked: Starship Flight 15, targeted for Nov 13, is set to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, the same load as Flight 14, per stories trending on X. SpaceX also announced a Qualcomm deal last week for its Starlink Mobile 5G rollout.
items.matters: Each Starship launch of V3 satellites adds far more network capacity than a Falcon 9 launch. That capacity is what Starlink's growth and pricing depend on.
items.know: The tab puts a Falcon 9 launch of 27 V2 Mini satellites at about 2.6 Tbps of downlink capacity, Flight 14's 26 V3 at about 26 Tbps, and a full Starship load of 60 V3 at about 61 Tbps. The 26 Tbps is Grok Bot's arithmetic from SpaceX's ~1 Tbps-per-V3 design figure. These are design capacities, not delivered user throughput.

items.title: Starlink revenue per subscriber per month
items.picked: Starlink users are complaining on X about bills rising by up to $36 in a year, with some plans hitting $156 a month under a new capacity-based pricing model. The story is trending alongside Musk's plans for space-based AI computing.
items.matters: Starlink is SpaceX's biggest business, and average revenue per user shows whether price hikes are offsetting the push into cheaper international and mobile plans. The trend had been steadily down.
items.know: Starlink's average revenue per subscriber was $69 a month in Q3 2026, up from $66 in Q1 and Q2 2026, the first rise in the tab's series. It was $99 in FY 2023, $91 in FY 2024 and $81 in FY 2025. The image is the Nov 2 export and stops at Q2 2026; the sheet now includes the Q3 figure.

items.title: SpaceX vs the rest of the world: orbital launches per year
items.picked: With Starship Flight 15 days away, stories trending on X note SpaceX's pace of 125 launches in 2026. SpaceX is also expanding at Starbase with a planned $24 billion AI supercomputer and power plant.
items.matters: SpaceX's launch share is the base of its moat in satellites, government work and the space data center plan. This chart shows how one company came to fly about half of the world's orbital launches.
items.know: The tab has SpaceX at 113 launches in 2026 to date vs 122 for the rest of the world, a 48.1% share, after 165 vs 159 (50.9%) in 2025 and 134 vs 125 (51.7%) in 2024. In 2010 SpaceX flew 2 of 74. The tab has no as-of date for the 2026 count, which is below the 125 cited on X today, so it looks a few weeks old.

items.title: SpaceX vs other listed space stocks since the SPCX IPO
items.picked: Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile report earnings after the close today. AST also unveiled its own reusable Blacklift rocket and a Rakuten joint venture last week, per stories trending on X.
items.matters: Since SpaceX listed, investors have had a direct way to own the space leader. This chart shows how the smaller space stocks have done next to it.
items.know: Rebased to 100 on Jun 11 2026, the tab's latest row (Nov 6 2026) has SPCX at 99.46, Rocket Lab at 46.24, AST SpaceMobile at 33.14 and Planet Labs at 36.73. So RKLB and ASTS have lost more than half their value while SPCX is about flat to its $135 IPO price. The image stops at Oct 30 and leaves out Planet Labs, and the sheet's Nov 4 to 6 dates show as raw serial numbers.

items.title: Anthropic's revenue vs what it spends on compute
items.picked: Anthropic's IPO roadshow is expected this week, with valuations now discussed at $1.1 to $1.3 trillion, and it has locked in $3.4 billion of Caterpillar gas generators for its data centers, per stories trending on X.
items.matters: IPO buyers will be paying for revenue growth, but compute is the biggest cost. Revenue per dollar of compute shows whether scale is improving the business.
items.know: Anthropic's Q3 2026 revenue was $16.956 billion against $9.863 billion of compute and infrastructure expense, or $1.72 per $1 of compute, down from 2.08x in Q2 ($11.555 billion vs $5.558 billion). In Q1 2025 the ratio was 0.40x. The figures are from the Nov 2 2026 amended S-1, and the image is a fallback render from the live sheet because the weekly Drive export has no PNG for this tab.

items.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI valuations from funding rounds
items.picked: Anthropic's IPO is expected to price at $1.1 to $1.3 trillion, down from talk of $2 trillion at the highs, as its roadshow gets going this week, per a story trending on X.
items.matters: The IPO will put the first public-market price on a frontier AI lab. This chart shows how fast private rounds marked these companies up.
items.know: In the tab's latest month, Sep 2026, Anthropic's last reported round valued it at $965 billion, above OpenAI's $852 billion; Anthropic passed OpenAI in May 2026. xAI was at $250 billion. Anthropic was at $61.5 billion as recently as March 2025. These are post-money round values as reported, and the tab ends in September, so it doesn't include IPO pricing talk.

items.title: CoreWeave's backlog vs quarterly revenue
items.picked: CoreWeave reports Q3 results after the close tomorrow, Nov 10, in a busy earnings week for AI clouds that also includes Nebius and Cerebras, per a story trending on X.
items.matters: CoreWeave's huge backlog is the main reason to own it, but it has to turn into revenue. The gap between the two is the number to watch on Tuesday.
items.know: At the end of Q2 2026, CoreWeave's backlog (remaining performance obligations) was $103.7 billion against $2.58 billion of quarterly revenue, about 40 times. Backlog was $14.7 billion in Q1 2025. The tab notes it includes OpenAI (about $22.4 billion total) and Meta contracts. Tomorrow's Q3 report will update both bars.

items.title: CoreWeave: quarterly revenue vs capex, and debt
items.picked: Ahead of CoreWeave's Nov 10 report, lenders are trimming data center exposure and AI-cloud stocks have sold off, per stories trending on X.
items.matters: CoreWeave is building with borrowed money, so how fast debt grows relative to revenue drives its risk. This chart puts the three side by side.
items.know: In Q2 2026, CoreWeave had $2.58 billion of revenue, $6.42 billion of capex and $35.55 billion of total debt. Capex peaked at $7.7 billion in Q1 2026, and debt has more than quadrupled from $8.03 billion at the end of 2024. The data ends with Q2 2026.

items.title: Neocloud quarterly revenue: CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN
items.picked: CoreWeave and Nebius both report this week, per a story trending on X previewing a heavy week of AI and space earnings.
items.matters: Revenue growth is what has to justify the debt-funded AI cloud buildout. This chart compares the biggest listed neoclouds.
items.know: In Q2 2026, CoreWeave's revenue was $2,575 million, Nebius $582.3 million and IREN $137 million. Nebius grew from $105.1 million in Q2 2025, more than five times. IREN's falling revenue reflects its bitcoin mining wind-down while AI cloud ramps. Data is as of Oct 12 2026, so Q3 is not in yet.

items.title: The AI chip scoreboard: data center revenue by company
items.picked: Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform with a $600 target this morning, citing data center revenue that nearly doubled year over year, while Nvidia's board probe of Jensen Huang is trending on X.
items.matters: Data center revenue is where the AI chip race is won or lost. This chart shows how far ahead Nvidia is and how fast the others are growing.
items.know: In the June 2026 quarter, the tab has Nvidia data center revenue at $89.02 billion, Broadcom semiconductor solutions at $20.84 billion, AMD data center at $6.72 billion and Intel data center and AI at $6.26 billion. AMD's figure more than doubled from $3.24 billion a year earlier. The tab stops at June 2026, so AMD's and Broadcom's latest reported quarters aren't in it.

items.title: Asia's AI chip exporters: Korea and Taiwan vs the S&P 500
items.picked: Taiwan's TAIEX jumped almost 5% today, its second-biggest daily gain on record, with MediaTek and Delta hitting limit-up and Korean chipmakers rallying too, per a story trending on X.
items.matters: Korea and Taiwan are the purest market bets on AI chips and memory. Their moves relative to the S&P 500 show when AI money is flowing into or out of Asia.
items.know: At the Oct 2026 month-end, the tab's latest point, Korea's ratio to the S&P 500 was 161.58 and Taiwan's 101.35 (Jan 2001 = 100), down from 191.42 and 112.14 in September. Korea's 2026 high was 218.41 in May. The data is monthly and ends in October, so today's rally isn't in it.

items.title: The midterm-year pattern: 2026 vs the average midterm year
items.picked: Stocks lost about $3 trillion the day after Democrats won both chambers in the Nov 3 midterms, and posts trending on X note that post-midterm periods have often brought rebounds.
items.matters: Midterm years have historically been weak until the election, then strong afterward. This chart compares 2026 with that pattern.
items.know: Through trading day 209, the tab's latest 2026 point, the S&P 500 was at 110.73 (prior year-end = 100), vs 97.99 for the average midterm year since 1974 and 105.81 for all years since 1971. 2026's low was 92.67 on day 60. The average midterm year ends at 101.86 and the all-years average at 110.12. The 2026 line stops before this week's post-election drop.

items.title: The Fed's 'supercore': services ex-shelter vs core and headline CPI
items.picked: October CPI comes out tomorrow, Tuesday Nov 10, with PPI on Friday, and traders on X say the data could reshape rate expectations after last week's selloff.
items.matters: Supercore inflation, services excluding shelter, is the measure the Fed watches for sticky price pressure. It tells you whether a hot headline number is about energy or something stickier.
items.know: In September 2026, the tab's latest month, supercore was 3.22% year over year, core 2.57% and headline 3.72%. Headline has run above core since March 2026, peaking at 4.17% in May, which points to energy and goods rather than services. The tab has no October 2025 row, a gap in the series.
